title: The first 30 minutes of an incident
purpose: A hurt person gets help before anything else, a missing phone is locked before it is worth anything to anyone, the right people hear inside the clock, nobody but Adham says a word to the client, and there is a written record, so one bad half hour never becomes a lost contract.
with: the site's Portfolio Manager on the floor, the quartermaster on the MDM, Mano for the claim, counsel, and the regulator, and Adham for every word to the client
when: The moment an injury or an incident reaches you, at any hour, on any day. Injuries and incidents reach you within 30 minutes: an injury from the Portfolio Manager, a theft or a checkpoint from the runner on the road, a hub outage from Mano, a client complaint from whoever it landed on, a ban wave from the Portfolio Manager, and a suspected minor from the Portfolio Manager when the site pushed the person on us. Friday is the day off, but the hotels run on their own lines and the hubs clear the factory phones, so your phone stays on.
takes: 30 minutes. The playbook for the specific incident carries the rest of the day.
needs: Your phone, charged, with every number that answers: the Portfolio Managers and their deputies, Mano, Adham, Youssef Medhat, the quartermaster, and the hub attendants
The incident playbooks page open: injury, theft or vehicle loss, police checkpoint, upload outage at a hub, power cut, an account ban wave, a suspected minor, a client complaint, a partner dispute
The dashboard and the MDM map, so you can see where every phone is and what it holds
The site plan for the site: its Portfolio Manager, the deputy written against that seat, and which hub it uses
Something to write on, with a clock in view

steps.do: Take the call and get the five things: which site, what happened, who is hurt or what is missing, how things stand right now, and who has already been called.
steps.detail: Let the caller finish, then ask for what is missing. For an injury: where, what happened, who is hurt, how they are, whether an ambulance was called. For a theft or a checkpoint: where the runner is, what happened or who is asking, the count on the manifest. For a complaint: who sent it, what it says, how it reached you. Get the number that will answer for the next half hour.
steps.check: You can say the site, the time, and what happened in one sentence, and you know who you will call back.

steps.do: If anyone is hurt, make sure the person comes first: recording stopped near them, site medical staff with them, an ambulance called if it is serious.
steps.who: The operator and the Portfolio Manager, on the floor
steps.time: Now, while you are still on the call
steps.detail: An injury overrides every rule, the cycle included. Nobody films an injury, and nobody waits for permission to call an ambulance. Ask the three questions in that order, and if any answer is no, have it done now while you hold the line. The Portfolio Manager gets to the site, stays with the person until medical staff take over, and keeps the floor calm.
steps.check: Someone is with the hurt person, medical staff or an ambulance are on the way, and nothing near them is recording.

steps.do: Stop the loss on the floor: filming stays off wherever it is unsafe, a banned or underage wearer is off the phone, and a site in a power cut keeps recording on battery.
steps.who: The Portfolio Manager, through the operators
steps.detail: A spot where someone got hurt stays off until it is made safe: PPE, cables, tethers on any elevated work. A wearer on a banned account, or one without an ID on file, sits down now and does not film again, not for one cycle. In a power cut the phones keep recording on battery; if the site itself has stopped work, tap stop, because idle footage is fraud. Say each of these to the Portfolio Manager as an instruction, not a question.
steps.check: Nothing is still being recorded that should not be, and nobody is still filming who should not be.

steps.do: Find and lock every missing phone: the quartermaster locates it on the MDM now and puts it in lost mode within the hour, and nobody wipes it.
steps.time: By minute 10, lost mode within the hour
steps.detail: Location tracking is on for every phone in transit, so use it. A locked phone is worth nothing to whoever has it, and a wiped phone can never be found, so the order is locate, lock, give it 24 hours, then wipe. A phone lost with footage on it is a suspected breach from the hour it went missing, and if we cannot show it was locked, the breach notice runs. Tell the site's Portfolio Manager what is coming back and when.
steps.check: Every phone on the manifest is on the MDM map or in lost mode, and nobody has wiped anything.

steps.do: Say it plainly to everyone on the call: nobody contacts the client, and nobody names the client to anyone.
steps.detail: Not to say sorry, not to explain, not to ask. Adham owns every word to the client. If a complaint or a question came in, it gets sent to you as it came, and the reply stays unwritten. If a site owner, an officer, or anyone else asks what the work is: video for a robotics research program, nothing more. Naming the client, even to a site owner, is immediate termination.
steps.check: The person the complaint or the question reached has heard from you that they do not reply, and nobody on the call will name the client.

steps.do: Take the outside calls yourself: the site owner, and the officer at a checkpoint.
steps.detail: The site owner hears about an injury from you, not from the floor. At a checkpoint you take the officer's call and confirm the runner, the company, and the count. Police, permits, a legal notice, or a held device go to Mano, who brings counsel and documents the visit the same day. A partner dispute is yours to settle on the operational side; the founders close anything about the terms.
steps.check: The site owner and any officer have heard from you, and anything held has a written receipt with the count, who holds it, and where.

steps.do: Open the playbook for this incident and read its list of who is told and by when.
steps.detail: Nine playbooks: injury, theft or vehicle loss, police checkpoint, upload outage at a hub, power cut, an account ban wave, a suspected minor, a client complaint, a partner dispute. A lost phone with footage on it runs the theft playbook plus the breach clock in the compliance manual. Each playbook ends with a list of names and clocks. That list is the decision, so do not make a new one in your head. If nothing fits, run the closest one and say so to Adham.
steps.check: You have named the playbook out loud and can list who it says to tell and by when.

steps.do: Call Adham yourself, at any hour, for any injury, for anything the client could see or hear, and for every line the playbook puts his name on.
steps.time: Within 30 minutes of an injury, the same hour for a client complaint or a lost phone with footage on it, the same day for the rest
steps.detail: Within 30 minutes of an injury: the Portfolio Manager calls Adham; check that it happened, and if it has not, make the call. The same hour: a complaint or any contact from the client, and a phone lost with footage on it, because his 24-hour clock to the client runs from the hour the company knew. The same day: a theft, a ban wave with the pattern and the fix, a partner dispute, hours lost to a power cut, and a hub outage in the executive sync, or the same hour once it passes 24 hours. A device held at a checkpoint, and a minor whose footage reached the client, go to Adham through Mano the same day. Give him five lines: the site, what happened, how the person or the phones are, what is being done, what you need.
steps.check: Adham has heard it from you, the Portfolio Manager, or Mano, inside the playbook's clock, and never from the client.

steps.do: Tell Mano within the hour when the incident touches the police, a claim, a replacement, a hub, or personal data, and the same day for a suspected minor.
steps.time: Within the hour; the same day for a suspected minor
steps.detail: Theft or a crash: Mano opens the insurance claim with the quartermaster, and the quartermaster sends replacements from the 10% spare pool before the next shift. A checkpoint that holds a device or a paper: Mano brings counsel. A hub outage reaches you from Mano: he owns the line and the ISP ticket, and you own the outcome. A lost phone with footage on it: Mano hears within the hour, because he and counsel notify the regulator within 72 hours. A suspected minor: the Portfolio Manager tells Mano the same day, always, because he holds every wearer's file; check that it happened. An injury: Mano gets it in the wrap report tonight for the paperwork and any insurance claim.
steps.check: Mano can say what he owns from this and by when.

steps.do: Tell everyone whose night just changed, the same hour: the Portfolio Managers, Youssef Medhat, and the quartermaster.
steps.detail: A hub down: every Portfolio Manager with a hub site hears the same hour, so their runners know where to drive, and every runner hears before leaving the site; the last run is still at the hub before 11 PM. Phones late from a checkpoint or a theft: the site's Portfolio Manager hears the same hour and plans without them. Footage that must be found or deleted, or a ban wave: Youssef Medhat, the same hour, with the site, the accounts, and the sessions. A count to run or spares to send: the quartermaster.
steps.check: Everyone whose plan changed has heard it from you, and nobody finds out from the road.

steps.do: Write it down while it is fresh, with a time next to every call.
steps.detail: The site, the time, what happened, who was there, who was told and when, what was done, what changed. Keep your own note of every call you made in these 30 minutes. The Portfolio Manager writes the full incident line for the wrap report tonight, and you log a checkpoint yourself: where, when, what was asked, what was shown, so runners on that road tomorrow know. That record is the company's defence if a clock is ever questioned.
steps.check: The note has a time next to every call, and it is on its way into the wrap report.

steps.do: Hand the rest to the playbook: put a name and a clock on every remaining line, and agree when you hear back.
steps.detail: Read the playbook's same-day, before-the-next-shift, and within-24-hours steps to the person who does each, and get a yes. Agree the time of the next call with the Portfolio Manager. The incident goes on the list for the executive sync tonight, where the escalations get cleared, and a complaint's follow-through goes in Adham's Sunday update.
steps.check: Every remaining line in the playbook has a name and a clock, the next call is agreed, and the incident is on tonight's sync.

done: The hurt person has help and the site is safe, every missing phone is locked and none is wiped, nobody but Adham has said a word to the client, Adham and Mano have heard what is theirs inside the clock, and the note is written with a time next to every call and a name on every remaining line of the playbook.

fails.if: The Portfolio Manager is unreachable and an operator calls you directly
fails.then: Take the call and run this page with the operator; the operator is standing next to the phone and the person. Keep calling the Portfolio Manager and take the book's calls yourself for the day. Send the deputy written against that seat to the site now, and if the Portfolio Manager is still silent by the wrap report, put the deputy on the book in writing tonight. Nothing on the floor pauses.

Leave the five lines by message: the site, what happened, how the person or the phones are, what is being done, what you need. Keep calling, and carry on with the playbook; the person, the phones, and the calls to Mano and the Portfolio Managers do not wait for him. The only thing that waits for Adham is a word to the client. If he is still silent and the 24-hour clock to the client is running, Youssif is his written deputy for the client, and nobody else speaks to them.

fails.if: Someone has already replied to the client, or has named the client
fails.then: Tell them to send nothing more. Get the exact words they sent, to whom, and when, and give them to Adham now, before the client replies, so he takes the conversation with the whole picture. Naming the client, even to a site owner, is immediate termination under the handbook; that conversation is Mano's, the same day, after Adham has the words.

fails.if: A phone with footage on it is missing and nobody can show it was locked
fails.then: It is a breach, and two clocks run from the hour the company knew. Lost mode now if it is not on already. Mano and you within the hour; Mano and Youssif establish what left, when, and how many people are in it, and Youssef Medhat pulls the sessions. Adham calls the client inside 24 hours. Mano and counsel notify the regulator inside 72. Nobody wipes for 24 hours, and nobody else calls the client or the regulator.

Not knowing is not a reason to wait. Run the first steps anyway: the person, the floor, the phones, nobody contacts the client, the note. Then call Adham the same hour and say you have no playbook; if it is not operations, money, or quality, it is his. Tell Mano the same day so the playbook gets written; the map is his.

fails.if: It reached you after the 30 minutes were already gone
fails.then: Start at the top the minute you hear. The clocks to Adham, Mano, and the regulator run from when the company knew, so they are already running. Write the delay in the note with who knew what and when. Take it up with the Portfolio Manager after the incident is handled, not during.

escalate: Adham, at any hour, within 30 minutes of an injury, the same hour for a client complaint or a lost phone with footage on it, and the same day for every other line with his name on it; Mano within the hour for the police, a claim, a hub, or personal data
